title: 1995 AHSME Problem 13
statement:
The addition below is incorrect. The display can be made correct by changing one digit \(d,\) wherever it occurs, to another digit \(e.\) Find the sum of \(d\) and \(e.\)

\[\begin{array}{rrrrrrr}&7&4&2&5&8&6\\+&8&2&9&4&3&0\\\hline1&2&1&2&0&1&6\end{array}\]

solutions.text: The units, tens, and hundreds columns work with carries \(0,\) \(1,\) \(1.\) In the thousands column, replacing every \(2\) by \(6\) gives \(6+9+1=16,\) so the result digit is also \(6.\) The next columns then give \(4+6+1=11\) and \(7+8+1=16,\) producing the corrected equation \(746586+869430=1616016.\) Thus \(d+e=2+6=8,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: Add from right to left and track each carry
Remember that the same replacement must be made at every occurrence of \(d\)
